events.title: Ford Introduces the Model T
events.description: Ford Motor Company began selling the Model T, a simple, durable and affordable car. Production later moved to the moving assembly line, which cut costs sharply.
events.significance: The Model T put car ownership within reach of ordinary families. It reshaped cities, work and daily life across the 20th century.

events.title: Damascus Falls to British and Arab Forces
events.description: Near the end of the First World War, British and Arab troops captured Damascus from the Ottoman Empire. The city had been a major Ottoman stronghold in the Levant.
events.significance: The capture marked the collapse of Ottoman power in the region. It set the stage for the postwar redrawing of the Middle East.

events.title: People's Republic of China Is Proclaimed
events.description: Communist leader Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the People's Republic of China in Beijing's Tiananmen Square. The announcement followed the communist victory in the Chinese Civil War.
events.significance: The founding began a new era for the world's most populous nation. The day is still marked each year as China's National Day.

events.title: Tuvalu Becomes Independent
events.description: The Pacific island nation of Tuvalu gained independence from the United Kingdom. It adopted its national flag the same day.
events.significance: Tuvalu became one of the world's smallest sovereign states. Its story now draws global attention to the threat that rising seas pose to low-lying nations.
